name: Cocos Islands Malay
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Adelaar & Prentice 1996 (cited on Glottolog coco1260); no online full text found; SIL/Cambridge blocked or 404

new_statements.quote: Similar to Indonesian (Soderberg & Olson 2008), stress in Cocos is predictable. Unaffixed words in isolation take primary stress on the penultimate syllable. But if the vowel in the penultimate syllable is a schwa /ə/, the stress is shifted to the ultimate syllable. Stress examples [ˈduʁi] duri 'thorn' [ˈut̪an] utan 'forest' [ˈakaɾ] akar 'root' [kəˈmaʁin] kemarin 'yesterday' [t̪əˈbu] tebu 'sugar cane'
new_statements.citation: Soderberg, Craig D. 2014. Cocos Malay (Illustrations of the IPA). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 44(1): 103-107. doi:10.1017/S0025100313000364
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of an unaffixed word spoken in isolation; if the penult vowel is schwa, stress moves to the final syllable (schwa-avoidance, as in Indonesian). Stress is predictable, i.e. non-contrastive.
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate schwa /ə/ shifts stress to the ultima ([kəˈmaʁin], [t̪əˈbu]). Statement is restricted to unaffixed words in isolation; affixed words are not discussed. The schwa clause makes a vowel-quality/weight-sensitive classification defensible if the catalog treats schwa-skipping penult systems that way.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, unaffixed words in isolation (citation forms); the transcribed North Wind passage marks stress on connected speech consistently with the rule. Speakers recorded in Kampung Cocos, Lahad Datu, Sabah, Malaysia (the Malaysian diaspora community), not on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands.
new_statements.identity_note: Soderberg 2014 describes Cocos Malay as spoken by the diaspora community in Sabah, Malaysia (Kampung Cocos, Lahad Datu district; speaker Adeka Bin Narel, age 64), explicitly 'focused exclusively on Cocos speakers in Malaysia', not the Cocos (Keeling) Islands community. Glottolog's coco1260 covers both (countries AU, CC, MY, SG), so the glottocode is the same; the home-islands variety is described only in Adelaar 1996 (not opened).

sources.note: p. 106, section 'Stress': stress is predictable; unaffixed words in isolation take primary stress on the penultimate syllable, shifted to the final syllable when the penult vowel is schwa; five examples given ([ˈduʁi] 'thorn', [ˈut̪an] 'forest', [ˈakaɾ] 'root', [kəˈmaʁin] 'yesterday', [t̪əˈbu] 'sugar cane'). Data from Cocos speakers in Kampung Cocos, Lahad Datu, Sabah (Malaysia). Full 5-page PDF was served by Cambridge Core without login; the landing-page HTML (saved) also carries the full text.
